    Three-armed stars with positive definite form #

    Proposition 4.1, Step 2 (periodic-mesh-calculations.tex): a star with three arms of L i + 1 vertices and ∑ (L i + 1)/(L i + 2) < 2 is D_n (two arms of one vertex) or E_6, E_7, E_8 (arms of 1, 2, 2, 1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 4 vertices).

    source
    theorem MultiplicativeBasisDeformations.frac_ge_half (n : ℕ) :
    1 / 2 ≤ (↑n + 1) / (↑n + 2)
    source
    theorem MultiplicativeBasisDeformations.frac_ge_two_thirds {n : ℕ} (h : 1 ≤ n) :
    2 / 3 ≤ (↑n + 1) / (↑n + 2)
    source
    theorem MultiplicativeBasisDeformations.frac_ge_three_quarters {n : ℕ} (h : 2 ≤ n) :
    3 / 4 ≤ (↑n + 1) / (↑n + 2)
    source
    theorem MultiplicativeBasisDeformations.frac_ge_five_sixths {n : ℕ} (h : 4 ≤ n) :
    5 / 6 ≤ (↑n + 1) / (↑n + 2)
    source
    theorem MultiplicativeBasisDeformations.three_arm_types (L : Fin 3 → ℕ) (hs : ∑ i : Fin 3, (↑(L i) + 1) / (↑(L i) + 2) < 2) :
    (∃ (a : Fin 3) (b : Fin 3), a ≠ b ∧ L a = 0 ∧ L b = 0) ∨ ∃ (a : Fin 3) (b : Fin 3) (c : Fin 3), a ≠ b ∧ a ≠ c ∧ b ≠ c ∧ L a = 0 ∧ L b = 1 ∧ 1 ≤ L c ∧ L c ≤ 3

    The three-armed stars of Proposition 4.1: D (two arms of one vertex) or E (arms of one, two and at most four vertices).
